channel.title: English — UpahJe.my
channel.description: Plain, sourced answers about technology for Malaysian small businesses.

item.title: CommandCode, OpenCode, DeepSeek: three different things
item.description: One is a paid CLI, one is a free CLI, one is an API. Their published prices, their drift, and one run that shows an exit code of zero is not success.

item.title: Google Business Profile: the fields that decide visibility
item.description: Google documents name rules, category rules, hours and what triggers suspension: what an SME should fix first, and the four fields that get restricted.

item.title: What a leaderboard row actually measures
item.description: SWE-bench and Terminal-bench score a model inside someone else's harness. The DeepSeek row is the example, and the run behind it has a reliability profile.

item.title: Where the same data gets typed three times
item.description: 97.2% of establishments use computers. The duplication sits between a digitised front office and a manual back office, and e-Invoice forces one record right.

item.title: What an AI agent can and cannot do for a Malaysian SME
item.description: An AI agent runs a loop on its own: reads a task, calls tools, checks, repeats. What that covers unattended, what needs a human, and what none should touch.

item.title: The e-Invoice threshold is now RM3 million
item.description: LHDN raised the e-Invoice exemption to RM3 million on 1 September 2026, freeing 1.1 million traders. What is required, what is not, and what is unpublished.

item.title: Your first automation should not be your worst process
item.description: Opinion. The process an owner hates most is often the worst to automate first: automating it removes evidence and hides the exceptions that decide the cost.

item.title: Agent harness, AI harness, agent framework: what they mean
item.description: An agent harness runs the loop: it executes tool calls, holds the transcript, applies permissions. Vendors say agent harness; AI harness is not their term.

item.title: Agent harnesses ranked: four CLIs installed on one machine
item.description: DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode scored 1-5 on five weighted criteria, using only what each showed us on 19 November 2026.

item.title: Automation work in Malaysia: the published rates
item.description: Thirty published prices for automation work from four Malaysian studios, one independent and one freelancer, checked November 2026. Some pages undated.

item.title: Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok: what differs
item.description: Scores settle little here. What you are stuck with is context window, price per token and documented capability, every cell sourced or marked not captured.

item.title: API or spreadsheet: which fits your volume
item.description: A spreadsheet wins at low volume with one owner; an API wins when two systems must sync. Three cases where a sheet is right, four signals it stopped scaling.

item.title: Where an API key goes in a harness, and where never
item.description: A harness reads your key from an environment variable or its store. What the key authenticates, four places it must never appear, and what to do if it leaks.

item.title: Agent harnesses: who makes them, what is open
item.description: Grok Bot and Dots are closed hosted products. OpenBot and MausBot are source-available, and only one is open source on its own licence; a licence row for each.

item.title: How to brief an automation job so you don't pay twice
item.description: Five things a freelancer needs before quoting, a reusable brief template, and the acceptance test to agree before work starts, written for a Malaysian SME.

item.title: Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Kimi: what the licence allows
item.description: Four open-weight families, five model cards, four licence shapes: MIT on DeepSeek, a custom Qwen licence, Mistral's own. What each permits and its rental cost.

item.title: Open or closed models: what an SME can run in-house
item.description: An open-weight model can be downloaded and run on hardware you control: cost per month in Malaysia, the volume where it beats per-call pricing, and the skills.

item.title: What RM100 a month buys you in AI, in Malaysia
item.description: RM100 buys a seat in a subscription app or a meter of API tokens. The Bank Negara rate of 19 November 2026, three usage levels, and where tokens win.

item.title: Five side-income skills in Malaysia that pay in 2026
item.description: Five skills clear a two-listing bar on the one Malaysian freelance platform whose public pages could be read, with rates, counts and dates from 11 listings.

item.title: What an agent harness is, and what it does with your request
item.description: A harness sits between you and the model: it holds the conversation, runs tools, sends each request and streams the answer. What one message looks like.

item.title: What is an API, for a Malaysian small business owner
item.description: An API is a contract that lets two systems exchange data without a human copying it. What it means for a Malaysian SME, open versus closed models, and the cost.
